text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.74% today to close at $139.48, continuing a three-day decline from its peak of $142.28 on November 13th. The stock's weakness comes despite oil prices holding steady around $89–$92 per barrel, suggesting the move reflects sector-specific headwinds rather than a broad energy market selloff. Escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—including Iran's reported attacks on U.S. military sites in Kuwait and warnings from the International Energy Agency about instability in the Strait of Hormuz—would normally support oil and energy stocks, but the market may be pricing in longer-term uncertainty about supply-chain reliability and global economic resilience.

The two-week decline of 3.4% reflects a broader consolidation after the stock hit $142 last week. With crude prices not falling significantly, the pullback likely signals investor caution: markets may be weighing whether Middle East tensions will persist as a structural drag on confidence and growth, rather than translate into a sustained oil-price premium that would benefit refiners and producers.
